result.note: Weekly roundup with thin detail; tested the defence-industry opening and the India–China hotlines and US sanctions, and skipped the Nepal disaster as lacking an institutional angle.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about developments in India's defence sector in the last week of August 2026:
items: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh broke ground on new warship yards.
Transfer of the technology of every conventional missile to private firms was approved.
Rolls-Royce offered India full ownership of fighter-engine technology.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are correct. Rajnath Singh broke ground on warship yards on 24 August, approved missile technology transfers to private firms on 26 August, and Rolls-Royce made its engine offer on 27 August. The fighter-engine technology is one that decades of state effort could not produce.
questions.source: Rajnath Singh broke ground on new warship yards on Monday, approved transfers of every conventional missile's technology to private firms on Wednesday, and by Thursday Rolls-Royce had offered India full ownership of the fighter-engine technology that decades of state effort could not produce.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's external relations in August 2026:
items: Ajit Doval and Wang Yi opened military hotlines along the India–China border after the two countries resolved their boundary dispute.
The United States sanctioned four Indian firms over Iranian oil.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong: the two hotlines, opened on 27 August, built a workable relationship around a dispute that remains unresolved. In the same week, Washington sanctioned four Indian firms over Iranian oil while Putin promised Delhi fuel and fertiliser.
questions.source: Doval and Wang Yi opened two military hotlines along the disputed border on Thursday, building a workable relationship around an unresolved dispute, even as Washington sanctioned four Indian firms over Iranian oil and Putin promised Delhi fuel and fertiliser.
